gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ND numbers and stop counts are not on the same scale. Stops = log2(ND number), so an ND2-400 variable ND tops out at 8.64 stops, yet makers list the same ND400 end as '8.6' (Urth), '9' (Hoya) or 'OD 2.7, 9 stops' (K&F, where OD 2.7 is really about ND500). Hoya says that near or at its maximum a cross-shaped dark pattern appears 'and cannot be eliminated', so the darkest stops on these labels can't be used cleanly. 1–5-stop VNDs (ND2-32) and PolarPro's preset 2–5 / 6–9-stop ranges are built so that the cross never shows.
standout_why: ChatGPT's run lists no search results and no cited pages, so there was no rival page to compare against. Its answer gives only a definition, fixed ND examples (ND8, ND64, ND1000) and the fixed-vs-variable split. It doesn't convert ND numbers to stops or optical density. It doesn't mention that variable NDs show an X or cross pattern at their darkest end, or that the 'ND2-400 / 9-stop' labels overstate the clean usable range. The finding is new, but it is unit conversion plus the makers' own warnings, not a measured test, so it scores 2 rather than 3.
decides: For video, where you can't fix a cross pattern later, it supports a 1–5-stop VND (ND2-32) such as the K&F Concept ND2-32 True Color that Dealectric already lists, or a preset range like PolarPro's 2–5 / 6–9 stops, over a wide 'ND2-400, 9-stop' filter. The extra headline stops on ND2-400 fall at the end that Hoya says shows an uncorrectable cross, and Urth says its ND2-400 is not recommended for wide-angle or telephoto lenses. A shopper who needs more than 5 stops should add a fixed ND, such as ND64 for 6 stops or ND1000 for about 10, rather than buy a wider VND.

findings.label: ND number → stops → optical density conversion
findings.value: 1 stop = ND2 = OD 0.3 (50% passes); 3 stops = ND8 = OD 0.9 (12.5%); 6 stops = ND64 = OD 1.8 (1.56%); 10 stops = ND1024, sold as 'ND1000', ≈ OD 3.0 (0.0977%)
findings.source_title: ND Filter Stops Chart: ND8, ND64 & ND1000 Explained (K&F Concept, dated 02 Nov 2026)
findings.note: Rows taken from K&F's table. K&F also warns that 'ND 0.9 refers to optical density, not 0.9 stops'. General rule: stops = log2(ND) = OD / 0.301.

findings.label: Variable ND ring markings are not calibrated in stops
findings.value: K&F: 'the marks around the ring are not necessarily calibrated as equal one-stop steps'
findings.source_title: ND Filter Stops Chart: ND8, ND64 & ND1000 Explained (K&F Concept)
findings.note: The same page suggests a way to check: lock ISO and aperture, then compare metered shutter times with and without the filter.

findings.label: Stated range vs normalised range
findings.value: K&F states 'OD 0.3 to 2.7 (1 to 9 stops)'. ND400 is really OD 2.60 = 8.64 stops; OD 2.7 would be about ND500 = 8.97 stops
findings.source_title: ND2-400 67mm Variable Neutral Density Filter Nano-Xcel
findings.note: The spec table contradicts the product name: log10(400) = 2.602 and log2(400) = 8.64. Price $79.99 (listed $99.99). The page also gives conflicting thread and cap sizes (67mm title, an FAQ saying 82mm).

findings.label: Stated range vs normalised range, and cross-pattern warning
findings.value: Hoya states '1.5 to 9 f-stops (ND3-400)'. Normalised: 1.58–8.64 stops. Hoya: near or at MAX 'a cross-like dark pattern will appear across the image and cannot be eliminated'
findings.note: The ND400 end is the same as Urth's, which Urth labels 8.6 stops, so Hoya's '9' is rounded up by 0.36 stop. Hoya also warns of vignetting below 24mm on full frame and below 13mm on APS-C, and says the filter needs a lens cap one size larger.

findings.label: Stated range and maker's lens restriction
findings.value: 1–8.6 stops. Urth: 'not recommended for use with wide-angle or telephoto lenses', and it points those users to its ND2–32, ND8–128 or ND64–1000 variable NDs or to fixed NDs
findings.note: Read through the storecheck tool (Shopify product data). Urth's other ranges match log2 exactly: ND2–32 = 1–5 stops, ND8–128 = 3–7, ND64–1000 = 6–10 (9.97).

findings.label: Stated range and cross-polarisation claim
findings.value: Two preset versions, 2–5 stops and 6–9 stops. PolarPro: 'Preset stop range eliminates any chance of cross-polarization'; 'Zero vignetting down to 16mm'. $149.99
findings.note: Read through the storecheck tool (Shopify product JSON, USD). The page doesn't give ND numbers. In ND terms 2–5 stops = ND4–ND32 and 6–9 stops = ND64–ND512.

findings.label: Maker's own stops-to-light wording is wrong
findings.value: PolarPro: '3-stops which filters out about half of the available light … 16.6-stops which let through only 1/32,000ths'. In fact 3 stops passes 1/8 (12.5%), 16.6 stops passes about 1/99,000, and 1/32,000 is about 15 stops. $99.99
findings.note: Read through the storecheck tool (Shopify product JSON). Arithmetic: 2^3 = 8, 2^16.6 ≈ 99,300, log2(32,000) ≈ 14.97.

findings.label: Reviewer test of an ND2-400 VND
findings.value: Keith Cooper (Northlight Images, 18 Dec 2015) measured a range of '1 to just over 8 stops', found the markings 'a rough guide at best', and saw 'a strange cross shaped darkening' at the max setting on a wide-angle lens. White balance shifted from 5050K to 4800K at the minimum setting
findings.source_title: MPB ND2-400 variable ND filter review (Northlight Images)
findings.note: This is a different brand from the candidates. Cooper is a named reviewer, but this is a hands-on test, not a lab measurement.
